description: A schematic map illustrates a typical estuary morphology, depicting the confluence of a river with a larger body of water, likely the sea. The image features a prominent green area representing land. A light blue, winding river originates from the upper part of the landmass and flows downwards, gradually widening before emptying into a larger, dark blue water body that occupies the lower right section of the map, representing the estuary and adjoining sea. Along the banks of the wider estuary, a light grey area is visible, which represents tidal flats or exposed sediment, characteristic of areas influenced by tides where sand or mud can appear at low tide. A red dashed line diagonally traverses the wider section of the estuary, crossing from one green landmass to the other. This line signifies a conceptual limit or cross-section, which, based on the context, likely represents the delineation between the estuary (CORINE Land Cover 8.3.2 Estuaries) and coastal waters (CORINE Land Cover 8.4.1 Coastal waters) based on the intended continuation of the coastline.
